Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
4:10 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying as easy as sending a message. You scan a code or type a number, approve with your PIN, and the money moves from your bank account in seconds. There is no card machine, no change to count and no waiting for a transfer to clear.

Here are the three main reasons:

It is quick and mostly free. Paying a friend or a shop usually costs nothing, and it works at any hour, even on holidays and Sundays.
It works almost everywhere. From a tea stall to a big mall, one printed code is enough. Small sellers don't need costly equipment, so more of them accept it every year.
One app, any bank. You can link several accounts and pay through whichever app you like, so you are never locked in to one bank.

Habit and trust did the rest. Banks and the government pushed it early, and once people used it for small things like vegetables or auto rides, they kept going. When most shops accepted UPI, carrying cash started to feel like extra effort. Want a few tips on keeping your UPI payments safe?

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
4:14 PM

Here is a relaxed 3-day Jaipur plan for your parents, with mornings for sightseeing and a rest after lunch.

Day 1, the old city: City Palace, Jantar Mantar and Hawa Mahal in the morning. Spend the afternoon at the Johari and Bapu bazaars for shopping and snacks, and have an early dinner.
Day 2, forts: Amber Fort early to beat the crowds and the heat. Stop at Jal Mahal for photos on the way back, rest at the hotel, then see Nahargarh Fort at sunset.
Day 3, easy and local: Albert Hall Museum, then Birla Mandir and a slow lunch. Finish with some last shopping for block-print textiles, jewellery and sweets.

A few tips: hire a car with a driver for all three days. Amber Fort has a steep walk, but jeeps run up to the top. Stay near the old city so the evenings are short trips. Late October and November are pleasant, though midday can still be warm.

Do your parents find lots of walking and stairs hard? I can then adjust the plan.
